signals.evidence: Alerts activated at night in many central communities following Iranian missile launch; heavy damage recorded in multiple locations including Petah Tikva, Givatayim, Bnei Brak, Tel Aviv.

Sergeant Boaz Tamam, wounded in Lebanon and lost his left leg, from his hospital bed: 'They are fighting with courage with many risks, but we will not give up. We must continue fighting until we restore the desired quiet to the residents of the north. We will do it, I am sure.'

Ministry of Health recommends sensitive populations and all public to avoid prolonged outdoor activity and strenuous physical activity in open air due to high air pollution expected to continue through Sunday.
IDF distributed updated combat schedule for upcoming months for 2026 war year; next recruitment cycle will replace current forces; mission duration set at approximately 9 weeks.

Ministry of Transport eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport starting Sunday: passenger quota increased from 50 to 80 per flight, plus 10 additional humanitarian cases, totaling up to 90 passengers per outgoing flight.

IDF briefing contradicted earlier public commitments by PM Netanyahu and Chief of Staff Zammir that Hezbollah would be disarmed; army stated disarming Hezbollah is not a war objective, causing anger among northern residents and requiring IDF clarification statement.
Significant damage caused to Aerosol aerospace manufacturing facility in Petah Tikva following Iranian missile strike; company announced substantial damage to its only manufacturing plant.
Aerosol aerospace manufacturing facility in Petah Tikva sustained significant damage from Iranian missile warhead; large crater and severe damage to surrounding buildings documented.
IDF reported Hezbollah rocket hit UNIFIL position in southern Lebanon, causing injury to three UN personnel, two in serious condition.

Many businesses resuming operations without waiting for war's end; 200 people sitting in restaurant without protected space; businesses understand compensation is meager and prefer to risk rather than follow guidelines.
Ministry of Health: More than 6,500 casualties evacuated to hospitals since start of war.
Ministry of Health recommended sensitive populations (elderly, pregnant women, children, chronic disease patients) avoid prolonged outdoor activity this weekend due to high air pollution forecast.

Reserve service for combat soldiers and support personnel extended from six weeks to nine weeks due to fighting in Lebanon; additional reservists required to staff other sectors including Syria, Gaza, and West Bank.
Starting Sunday April 5, passenger numbers per flight from Ben Gurion will increase from 70 to 80 or 90 passengers, including approximately 20 humanitarian and medical cases.

Tel Aviv police district decision to disperse Saturday anti-government protest at Habima Square was made following pressure from district officers on junior officer, not from senior Home Front Command officials; officers falsely announced decision was based on Home Front Command assessment when no formal assessment occurred.

Sergeant N., tank crew member in southern Lebanon: 'In general, we are here in a defensive mission on the northern border, in the southern Lebanon sector, and we are here to strengthen the residents of the north and protect them.'

Ministry of Health: Since start of Operation 'Roaring of the Lion', 6,594 casualties evacuated to hospitals as of Friday April 3, 2026 at 7:00 AM; 125 currently hospitalized (2 critical, 14 severe, 24 moderate, 79 mild, 1 anxiety, 5 under medical evaluation).

Three impact zones in Qiryat area: vehicles caught fire after interception debris near residential building, direct hit caused damage to building facade, parked vehicles damaged by shrapnel; no casualties reported.

IDF changed reserve unit deployment schedule due to ongoing war with Iran; reservists required to serve longer than originally planned; some reservists' missions advanced with new Order 8 effective dates.

Couple from Ramat Gan: 'We follow the guidelines and when we received the alert, we went out in the middle of the night to the car and drove to the shelter. When we were in the shelter we heard a strong explosion, but we didn't know there was a hit in our house. Only when we returned did we see the extensive destruction in the house.'

Ramat Gan municipality head emphasized: following guidelines saved lives; couple who evacuated to shelter when alert sounded survived direct hit on their home; house sustained severe damage but residents were safe.

IDF Spokesperson: 'IDF detected missiles launched from Iran toward Israeli territory minutes ago. Defense systems working to intercept threat. Home Front Command distributed preliminary alert directly to mobile phones in relevant areas. Public requested to show responsibility and follow guidelines—they save lives. Enter protected spaces when alert received, remain until new notice. Exit only after explicit instruction.'

Cinema City chain reopened movie theaters after more than a month with capacity of up to 50 people per theater; Planet and Lev cinemas in Tel Aviv, Raanana, and Alon Yehuda also reopened in limited format per Home Front Command guidelines.

Ministry of Health recommended all public minimize strenuous physical activity in open air; sensitive populations (elderly, pregnant women, children, chronic disease patients especially heart and respiratory) avoid prolonged outdoor activity due to high to very high air pollution forecast through Friday-Saturday evening.

Health system preparing for scenarios of casualties, overload, and patient evacuation; significant reinforcement of Magen David Adom forces in Dead Sea area; expanded logistics and operational capabilities; increased teams operating 24/7 with additional intensive care vehicles; additional vehicles and teams added to ensure rapid and continuous response to medical events.

Director of Religious Services Ministry sent stern letter to Rabbi of Western Wall regarding Rashbi site in Meron operating in full routine contrary to Home Front Command guidelines; site open to public without Home Front Command approval; ministry demanded immediate compliance with guidelines or closure.

Northern municipal leaders (Lobby 1701): 'Northern residents are abandoned by the State of Israel. The decision to back down from the goal of disarming Hezbollah guarantees one thing: the next round is around the corner.' Mayors Avihai Stern (Kiryat Shmona), David Azulay (Metula), Assaf Langalben (Upper Galilee Regional Council): 'Prime Minister, it is time you start giving answers. Time to end years of abandonment of northern residents, to strive for real decision and not buy temporary false quiet that endangers our children's future and the Galilee's future.'

Supreme Court hearing: Justices Yitzhak Amit, Khaled Kabub, and Yechiel Kasher stated unequivocally that political protest freedom does not disappear during war and requires enhanced protection; police must work with Home Front Command to enable protests; court clarified police responsibility to find ways to facilitate demonstrations.
Clashes between police and residents in Rahat during police operation against property crime; stones thrown at patrol unit; riot dispersal measures used; four suspects arrested.

War added approximately 15,000 wounded to rehabilitation department; one in five Israelis defined as person with disability; most apartments in Israel not adapted even for basic accessibility; housing shortage for disabled persons including wounded soldiers.

Organization 'Kavim' (Directions) working to help wounded soldiers and disabled persons achieve independence; focus on accessible housing design including ramps, elevators, wide doors, accessible bathrooms, and protected spaces adapted for mobility-impaired individuals.
Missile with cluster warhead fired from Iran. Two people lightly wounded in Petah Tikva, one person lightly wounded in Matzkereth Batya from broken glass.

Rabbi Shlomi Matot: 'We see the people of Israel in its greatness' and 'Everyone helped with preparations and asked many questions. The feeling is that everyone wants the holiday to be preserved in the best way.'
Cluster warhead missile fired at Haifa and Kariyat Ata. Heavy damage to buildings and vehicles in Haifa and Kariyat Ata. No casualties reported at time of article.
IDF announced reserve service extended from 6 weeks to 9 weeks for 2026 due to ongoing war.
Health Ministry issued guidance recommending vulnerable populations avoid prolonged outdoor activity and strenuous exercise due to high air pollution forecast for April 3-4.
Transportation Ministry eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport: passenger quota increased from 50 to 80, plus 10 humanitarian cases, effective Sunday.

Home Front Command emphasized responsibility on hikers to check for protected spaces at hiking sites before departure and provided specific protective instructions: move to road edges, distance from vehicles, lie on ground protecting head.
Health Ministry issued urgent notice recommending vulnerable populations avoid prolonged outdoor activity and strenuous exercise due to high air pollution forecast for April 3-4.
Google deployed visual map display directly in Android emergency alerts showing threat zones, eliminating need to unlock device and open external apps—reducing response time in emergencies.
Alerts activated in multiple communities across central Israel and Sharon region following Iranian missile fire, indicating residents received and responded to warnings.
Health Ministry: Since start of Operation Lion's Roar, 6,594 injured evacuated to hospitals; currently 125 hospitalized (2 critical, 14 severe, 24 moderate, 79 mild).
Health Ministry issued guidance recommending vulnerable populations avoid prolonged outdoor activity and strenuous exercise due to high air pollution forecast for April 3-4.
Transportation Ministry eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport: passenger quota increased from 50 to 80-90 per flight, effective Sunday, based on security assessments.
Iranian missile fire caused shrapnel falls in Ramat Gan, Petah Tikva, Givat Shmuel, and Beni Brak. One person lightly wounded in Ramat Gan.

Environmental Protection Ministry and Health Ministry issued guidance recommending vulnerable populations avoid strenuous outdoor activity due to high air pollution from dust transport from North Africa.
IDF announced reserve service extended from 6 weeks to 9 weeks for current and next reserve cycles due to operational needs and manpower requirements.
Health Ministry: Since start of Operation Lion's Roar, 6,594 injured evacuated to hospitals; 125 currently hospitalized (2 critical, 14 severe, 24 moderate, 79 mild, 1 anxiety, 5 under evaluation).
Simultaneous rocket barrages from Lebanon and Iran caused shrapnel falls in Kariyat Ata and surrounding areas. Material damage to buildings, vehicles, and water networks reported.
Transportation Ministry eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport: passenger quota increased from 50 to 80 per flight, plus humanitarian cases, effective Sunday.

Magen David Adom: In past 24 hours, 26 people treated (12 physical injuries, 14 panic cases). Since start of Operation Lion's Roar: 2,250 treated (1,757 physical injuries, 493 panic cases); 550 from missile impacts including 19 killed.
Health Ministry issued guidance recommending vulnerable populations avoid prolonged outdoor activity and strenuous exercise due to high air pollution forecast for April 3-4.
Iranian ballistic missile with cluster warhead dispersed submunitions over Haifa. Several vehicles caught fire in Kariyat Ata. Man in his 70s sustained light shrapnel wounds.
Transportation Ministry eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport: passenger quota increased from 50 to 70 per flight, plus up to 20 humanitarian cases, effective April 5.
Transportation Ministry eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport: passenger quota increased from 50 to 80 per flight, plus 10 humanitarian cases, effective April 5.
Health Ministry warned that April 3-4 would see high to very high air pollution across the country and recommended vulnerable populations avoid prolonged outdoor activity and strenuous exercise.
Health Ministry: 148 injured hospitalized in past 24 hours from Iran war; total hospitalizations exceed 6,500. Five under medical evaluation, 31 treated for anxiety.
Arab Israeli man indicted for compiling reports on missile damage and casualties for foreign agent, including information on water, electricity, internet outages, and emigration rates.
Transportation Ministry eased flight restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport: passenger quota increased from 50 to 70, plus 20 humanitarian cases, bringing maximum to 90 per flight, effective Sunday.
Iranian ballistic missile struck Neot Hovav industrial zone south of Beersheba, sparking fire. No injuries or hazardous material involvement reported.
Iranian ballistic missile with cluster warhead dispersed submunitions across central Israel, hitting multiple Tel Aviv area cities and causing damage. No immediate injuries reported.

Hezi Ben-Yakar about his brother Effi, IDF reservist: 'He was a person who loved to contribute, always saw the other before him. Every task, every request, his friends and family always came first.' Effi's organs saved four lives.

Parent: 'My six-year-old daughter loves it. She sings it happily, over and over... But the song is about Iranian drones in the sky. That is what I cannot shake.' Describes children taking shelter multiple times, toddlers excited by sirens, children knowing how to reach safe rooms alone.

Over 2,000 people from Beersheba displaced from homes damaged by rockets and cluster bombs, placed in hotels for limited periods. Received eviction notices day before Seder despite homes still uninhabitable.
Shlomi Mayor Gabi Naaman and local council organized large community Seder, inviting residents from neighboring hard-hit communities to participate.

Iranian missile barrage on northern Israel. Man in his 70s lightly wounded by missile fragments in Kariyat Ata. Multiple shrapnel fall sites in Haifa area; at least 10 sites investigated by emergency services.

Micha Katz, IDF veteran with PTSD, leading demonstrations across Knesset with other soldiers. Over 80 soldiers with PTSD have committed suicide since Oct. 7, not including pre-Oct. 7 suicides or Supernova survivors.

Parent of autistic son Danny: 'I want to stay in the car!' said Danny, who was terrified when sirens sounded. 'His face was white and he was terrified.' Danny lacks judgment to understand he must leave car during missile attack.
Iranian missile fire caused sirens across Israel throughout Friday night. Reported falls in central and southern Israel with damage to industrial zone in Negev. No casualties reported.
Israel's Health Ministry: 6,594 wounded people evacuated to hospitals since war start; 125 currently hospitalized including 2 critical, 14 serious, 24 moderate, 79 lightly wounded

Moshe Davidovich, head of Mateh Asher Regional Council: 'If the statements made in the army's briefing are accurate, we see this shift as a resounding slap in the face to residents who have remained in their homes since the start of the war, effectively serving as a human shield for Israel'
Asaf Langelben, head of Upper Galilee Regional Council: 'without disarming the group, northern residents would continue to live under the threat of rockets and ongoing cycles of security escalation'
Sirens sounded across central Israel after Iranian missile launch; residents sought shelter as air defenses were activated
Cluster missile hit Kiryat Ata; elderly man injured by debris; extensive destruction with vehicles engulfed in flames and residential buildings damaged
Starting Sunday, Ben Gurion Airport passenger quota on outgoing flights increased from 50 to 70 passengers, with up to 20 additional humanitarian cases allowed, total cap 90 per flight

Passover event in Jerusalem brought together families who lost homes in missile attacks, survivors from Gaza captivity, serving soldiers, and Holocaust survivors; event framed as expression of Jewish resilience across generations
Rocket fire from Lebanon and missiles from Iran struck northern Israel; direct hit recorded at parking lot in Nahariya; building hit in Gesher HaZiv; damage reported at both sites

Black market for prescription drugs operating via Telegram channels ('The Good Doctor', 'The Health Channel', 'Dr. Dobi', 'The Central Pharmacist') supplying sedatives, sleeping pills, ADHD medications, and opioids through unregulated channels
Air raid alerts activated in multiple waves across Galilee, Haifa and surrounding areas; Home Front Command instructed residents to remain in protected spaces before announcing safe to leave shelters
Air raid sirens sounded across central Israel and Samaria following Iranian missile launch; millions of Israelis sent into shelters
Impact sites reported in Bnei Brak, Givat Shmuel, Petah Tikva, and industrial area in Negev following Iranian missile strikes

Musical morning prayers held at Zefat Academic College during Passover intermediate days, broadcast live due to security situation; organizers stated: 'We are in moments of elevation and unity. Despite the limitations and physical challenges, the voice rising now from Tzfat is one of unbreakable faith'

Iranian cluster missile struck central Israel; heavy damage caused to buildings in Petah Tikva with large crater at impact site; a man and woman lightly injured in Petah Tikva, another person lightly injured in Mazkeret Batya by blast wave
Iranian cluster missile struck Haifa area; heavy damage reported at multiple impact sites; vehicles caught fire; 79-year-old suffered light injuries from rocks thrown by blast

Defense Minister Israel Katz: 'Israel's policy in Lebanon has been and remains clear: The supreme objective is the disarmament of Hezbollah through military and diplomatic means. The IDF will maintain security control in the Litani area, and the return of approximately 600,000 residents of southern Lebanon will not be permitted south of the Litani until the security of northern residents is ensured'

IDF announced reserve duty extended to approximately nine weeks; updated Tzav 8 emergency call-up notices issued; applies to upcoming call-ups and forces currently deployed across all units and branches
